newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Twelve bids for Dar es Salaam hotel.
newsitem.headline: Twelve bids for Dar es Salaam hotel.

text.p: Twelve companies have bid for a 75 percent stake in the state-owned Kilimanjaro Hotel in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania's privatisation authority said.

The companies include two East African hotel chains -- Serena Lodges and Sopa Lodges -- India's Taj Group, the Hainan corporation of China, South African-based Stock Hotels and Resorts, U.S-based Gencom Corp and Feram Holdings of Gibraltar.

The deadline passed last Friday for bids for the eight-storey hotel, which occupies a prime site overlooking Dar es Salaam harbour. Once regarded as the city's premier hotel, it fell on hard times, like many other state assets.

The Parastatal Sector Reform Commission (PSRC), which is handling the privatisation, said it expected the winning bidder to enter into an agreement with a major international management group such as Hilton, Holiday Inn or Marriott.
A technical committee is evaluating the bids and a shortlist of three preferred bidders will soon be called on to make a presentation before the PSRC.
Final negotiations will lead to a memorandum of understanding, followed by a formal sales agreement.
